question: What will be the nationwide wastewater detection category of RSV on December 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: WWSCAN's national RSV category stays LOW until the network reaches seasonal onset, then usually jumps to MEDIUM/HIGH. Reference seasons: on ~Dec 1, 2025 it was LOW (all sites in offset; it was HIGH by the December 2025 update). In 2024-25 onset came in early December, right at the boundary. 2023-24 was earlier (from memory). October 2026 detection was ~18% vs 15.2% in October 2025, a bit ahead of a slow year, with the South picking up. Medium gets some mass as a transition state. No human market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the WastewaterSCAN dashboard's national RSV category when Metaculus checks on/after 2026-12-01, not off CDC NWSS. Not Detected/Not Calculated resolves Other.
- Mechanism (WWSCAN monthly updates): RSV is a 'seasonal pathogen'. A site or the nation stays LOW 'due to not being in seasonal onset'. After onset, the category is based on concentration and typically goes to MEDIUM/HIGH quickly.
- Oct 2026 update (published 2026-11-02): national LOW, not in onset. Detection ~18% of samples in Oct 2026, up from ~9% in Sep. Median concentration below the limit of detection. Pickup at Southern sites; other regions mostly non-detect.
- Oct 2025 update: national LOW, detection ~15.2%, mostly in the South, offset.
- Nov 2025 update (published ~early Dec 2025): national LOW, all sites in seasonal offset, detection ~34% in Nov 2025.
- Dec 2025 update: national HIGH, >50% of sites in onset. Of 147 sites: 38 LOW, 6 MED, 77 HIGH, 26 insufficient data. The 2025-26 season started slower than 2024-25.
- 2024-25: network onset in early December 2024 and peak in late Jan/early Feb 2025. As of 2024-11-13 a few CA sites were HIGH (in onset) and others LOW.
- 2023-24 season was earlier (background knowledge, not verified this run).
- Status quo as of 2026-11-05: LOW.
- Event window: single check on/after 2026-12-01. As of 2026-11-05 ~26 days remain until the check.
- Searched for but not found: the exact national onset rule (e.g. % of sites), daily dashboard values for Nov 2026, and any prediction market (none found).
calls.reference_class: WastewaterSCAN national RSV category on ~Dec 1 in past seasons (2023-2025), as determined by timing of network-wide seasonal onset

calls.reasoning: WastewaterSCAN assigns RSV 'LOW' automatically until seasonal onset (all samples in a 14-day lookback >=2,000 copies/g); after onset the category combines level and trend. National onset came in early Dec 2024; in 2025 RSV was still LOW with sites in offset per the Nov update (published Dec 5) and HIGH by the Dec update. Oct 2026 detection ~18% vs ~15% in Oct 2025: a similar or slightly earlier pace, with the South picking up. Dec 1 sits at the onset cusp, so LOW is the status quo with substantial mass on a jump to HIGH/MEDIUM. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi none).
calls.dossier:
- Category rules (data.wastewaterscan.org/about): RSV onset = first day all samples in 14-day lookback >=2,000 copies/g; offset = only 50% >=2,000 copies/g; in offset/non-onset RSV is assigned LOW; once in onset, standard trend+level rules over the preceding 21 days apply.
- Oct 2026 update (published 2026-11-02): national RSV LOW, 'due to not being in seasonal onset'; detection ~18% of samples in Oct vs ~9% in Sep; concentrations/detections 'starting to pick up at sites across the South'; most sites still consistent non-detects.
- Same update: influenza A HIGH, onset ~4 weeks earlier than 2025-26 (season timing context; RSV and flu are not necessarily synchronized).
- Oct 2025 update (published 2025-11-03): RSV LOW, detection ~15.2%, concentrations below detection limit nationally for 3 weeks, lower than 2024 at the same time.
- Nov 2025 update (published 2025-12-05): RSV LOW, 'all sites in seasonal offset'; detection ~34% in Nov 2025, mostly the South; notes the network hit RSV onset in early December 2024 (2025-26 was slower).
- Dec 2025 update: RSV HIGH, >50% of sites in onset, detection ~69%, median ~7,148 copies/g, upward trend.
- Jan 2026 update: RSV HIGH, downward trend.
- Status quo: LOW (not in onset as of the Nov 2 update).
- Implied component rates: given national onset by Dec 1, past post-onset readings were HIGH (2025-26 Dec); MEDIUM possible early in a wave. Given no onset, LOW is deterministic.
- Resolves off the WastewaterSCAN dashboard's national RSV category as checked on or after 2026-12-01 (backup: monthly ghost.io update), not off CDC NWSS levels. Not Detected/Not Calculated -> Other.
- Event window: single-point reading on/after 2026-12-01; as of 2026-11-05 about 26 days remain before the check.
- Searched, not found: the live dashboard's current national RSV category/site onset share (JS dashboard not readable); the exact Dec 1, 2024 category; any human prediction market (none found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).
calls.reference_class: WastewaterSCAN national RSV category around Dec 1 in recent seasons (2024: onset early Dec; 2025: LOW at ~Dec 1, HIGH by mid/late Dec)

calls.reasoning: WastewaterSCAN keeps the national RSV category at LOW until the network reaches seasonal onset; after onset the category comes from trend plus level and usually goes to MEDIUM or HIGH. The Nov 2, 2026 update (October data) shows LOW, most sites non-detect, 18% detection (Sep 9%) and the South starting to rise. In 2025 the category was still LOW on Dec 5, then HIGH by Jan 8; in 2024 onset came in early December. October 2026 detection is slightly above October 2025 (15.2%), so the season looks a little earlier than 2025 but not clearly 2024-like. LOW stays the modal outcome; onset landing just before Dec 1 is the main path to MEDIUM or HIGH. No human market found: the harness found none on Polymarket or Manifold, and Kalshi and bookmakers were not separately searched.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the WastewaterSCAN dashboard national RSV category when Metaculus checks on or after 2026-12-01; the monthly wwscan.ghost.io update is the backup source. Not Detected or Not Calculated resolves as Other.
- Event window: a single snapshot on or after 2026-12-01. As of 2026-11-05, about 26 days remain.
- Method (WWSCAN monthly posts, 2025): categories combine the 21-day trend, the level (national tertiles over 365 days) and detection frequency. RSV is treated as a seasonal pathogen: the national category is LOW while sites are in seasonal offset, and after onset it is set by trend plus level.
- Oct 2026 update (published 2026-11-02): national LOW; RSV detected in about 18% of October samples (September about 9%); median concentration below the limit of detection; most sites have consistent non-detects; concentrations starting to rise in the South; other regions minimal; WWSCAN calls this typical seasonal timing, not exceptionally early.
- Oct 2025 update (published 2025-11-03): national LOW, all sites in offset; detection about 15.2%; 134 sites Low, 0 Medium, 1 High, 12 insufficient data; levels lower than the same period in 2024.
- Nov 2025 update (published 2025-12-05): national LOW, all sites in offset; November detection about 34%, mostly in the South; 115 sites Low, 2 Medium, 15 High, 15 insufficient data.
- Dec 2025 update (published 2026-01-08): national HIGH; December detection about 69%; says the network reached onset in early December 2024 and peaked in early January 2025; calls the 2025-26 start slower than 2024-25.
- So in 2025 the national category was LOW through at least Dec 5 and HIGH by early January. For 2024 the exact Dec 1 dashboard category was not found (the Nov and Dec 2024 posts returned 404).
- Searched but not found: a dashboard snapshot from November 2026, the exact national onset threshold rule, and the Dec 1, 2024 category. No prediction market found.
calls.reference_class: WastewaterSCAN national RSV category around Dec 1 in recent seasons (2024: onset early Dec, Dec 1 status not confirmed; 2025: LOW through Dec 5, HIGH by early Jan)

calls.reasoning: WastewaterSCAN assigns RSV LOW nationally until seasonal onset (more than 50% of sites in onset), then uses level plus trend. On about Dec 1 in 2025 it was LOW, and in 2024 onset came in early December. October 2026 detection (about 18%) is only slightly ahead of 2025 (about 15%), so onset before the check is plausible but less likely than not. If onset arrives, a rising trend favors HIGH over MEDIUM. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the facts: LOW until national onset, LOW on Dec 5 2025, network onset in early December 2024, and October 2026 detection of about 18% vs about 15.2% in 2025. The only factual gap, the Dec 1 2024 category, cannot be settled offline; since onset came in early December 2024, it was likely LOW or at the edge. The remaining disputes are judgment: the onset probability (I put it at about 35%) and the MEDIUM vs HIGH split after onset (HIGH favored, given December 2025 site counts of 77 HIGH vs 6 MEDIUM). I carried forward the runs' reference class.
